content.title: Default Browser Actions and Control
content.hook: Browsers have their own behavior for certain interactions. A form submission, for example, has a default action.
content.context: When you need the page to handle an interaction itself, you may need to stop that default action.
goals: Understand that some browser events have built-in behavior and learn when `preventDefault()` is appropriate for a controlled page interaction.

content.title: The key method

content.question: Why would a form handler call `event.preventDefault()`?

options.text: To stop the browser's default submit action so the page can handle the interaction itself.
To make the browser load CSS faster.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. To stop the browser's default submit action so the page can handle the interaction itself.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. To stop the browser's default submit action so the page can handle the interaction itself.

content.title: Compare the flows
content.text:
Without `preventDefault`, the browser may continue with its normal form submission behavior.

With `preventDefault`, your handler can keep control of the interaction and update the current page instead.

content.title: Try it
A caution
content.text:
`preventDefault()` is not a magic "make this secure" method. It only controls the browser's default action for the event.

It also does not validate whether a user is allowed to perform an operation. Security boundaries are handled elsewhere and will be taught later.

options.text: `preventDefault()` stops the default action for the particular event being handled.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. `preventDefault()` stops the default action for the particular event being handled.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. `preventDefault()` stops the default action for the particular event being handled.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Some browser events come with default behavior. An event handler can intentionally prevent that default when the page needs to take control.
**Senior habit:** Ask what the browser would do by default before deciding whether your handler should override it.
